item.title: Need to vent and family is burdened enough. So you guys have been chosen.
item.description:
Today I talked to a lawyer about my end days and what needs to be done before my expiration date. I have stage four colon cancer and I just spent three weeks in the hospital because the cancer and the chemo destroyed my blood cells. It was so bad my brother came down to say goodbye. My oncologist told him I might not make it through the weekend. The hospital and all the staff did a great job keeping me alive but man am I messed up. Got appointment with oncologist on Monday to explore my options but quality of life comes before length of life. I just had to put my wife in a mental care facility so now I'm in the house alone except for my cat. Will have to sell my house to cover her care. Needed to anyway because I'm going to need one room on the first floor. Stairs are hard right now. When it rains it pours. I would appreciate some positive vibes and a little love.
My support cat. Elvis. The snuggle is like a drug.

item.description: You buy it, you own it. Period... One of the biggest problems with digital gaming is that buying a game doesn’t always mean you own it forever. Many digital purchases are technically licenses, meaning publishers can restrict access or shut down online features, sometimes leaving players unable to enjoy games they’ve already paid for. The proposed Power to the Players Act aims to change that by strengthening ownership rights and protecting access to purchased games. Do you think publishers should be legally required to keep games playable after shutting down their servers?

item.title: America Has Bulletproof Backpacks, Active Shooter Drills, and Apparently No Fucking Idea What the Problem Is.
item.description:
A little school desk. A backpack. A drawing of a happy family. And a shadow that no child should ever have to live under. Somewhere along the way, America decided that preparing children to survive gun violence was easier than preventing it.
Think about how utterly insane that is. Children learn their ABCs, multiplication tables, and where to hide if someone enters their classroom with a gun. We call it an active shooter drill. As though giving a nightmare an official name somehow makes it normal. Every time another child dies, the same machinery springs into action. Thoughts and prayers. Flags at half-mast. Politicians looking solemn. And then the national conversation moves on until the next collection of tiny shoes is left behind. We're told the answer is more security. More armed guards. More surveillance. More fortified entrances. Apparently, the American dream now includes sending your six-year-old to a building designed like a fucking military installation. And here's the contradiction. A country that celebrates individual freedom has somehow accepted a reality where children must rehearse the possibility of being murdered at school. Whose freedom are we actually protecting? And who is paying the price? There are serious debates to be had about constitutional rights, gun ownership, enforcement, mental health, and public safety. But pretending that nothing can be done is not a policy. It's a political choice dressed up as helplessness. The artwork doesn't need a politician, a slogan, or a statistic. Just an empty desk. A child's drawing. A red crayon. And the shadow of a weapon where a child's future should have been. Sometimes the absence of a child says more than a thousand speeches. Children should be worrying about homework, scraped knees, friendships, and what they're having for lunch. Not whether they'll make it home. A society's priorities aren't revealed by what it claims to value. They're revealed by what it repeatedly allows its children to endure. THE EMPTY DESK IS NOT THE PRICE OF FUCKING FREEDOM. #GunViolencePrevention #SchoolSafety #ProtectOurKids #GunReform #EnoughIsEnough #AmericanPolitics #PoliticalArt #StreetArt #StencilArt #ChildrensRights #NeverAgain #Imgur
